sections.context: Warren already enforces a USD spend cap per run: src/runs/cost-cap.ts (coerceCostCap/readMaxCostUsd/resolveCostCapUsd/isOverBudget) and the event bridge (src/runs/stream/) cancels the burrow run when cumulative turn_end cost crosses maxCostUsd. runs.cost_usd + tokens_* are populated post-hoc. This plan adds a TOKEN dimension: per-run budget with 90% regular / 10% reserve split, maxBadAttempts, early-exit on confident completion, per-tool token accounting in run events. Files: src/runs/cost-cap.ts, src/runs/stream/*, src/db/migrations for any new columns, src/runs/cost-analytics.ts.
sections.approach: Build ON the existing cost-cap machinery - same module family, same bridge enforcement point. Token accounting already arrives in telemetry events (tokens_input/output/cache fields seen in runs). Compute cumulative tokens per turn_end like the cost path, compare against a token budget resolved from the same rendered_agent_json frontmatter (key: maxTokens, default null = unlimited). Reserve: terminate only when cumulative tokens exceed budget*0.9 AND the last turn was NOT a confident completion signal (agent-reported done); the 10% reserve exists to let a finishing turn complete. maxBadAttempts: count consecutive failed tool_use turns (tool_result with error); terminate at the cap. Per-tool accounting: emit a run event kind='budget.tokens' per tool_use with the tool name + delta. Keep all decisions in a pure module (mirror cost-cap.ts style) so tests are deterministic.
steps: Extend src/runs/cost-cap.ts family: add token budget resolution (readMaxTokens, resolveMaxTokens, isOverTokenBudget) with the same fail-open coercion as coerceCostCap (malformed -> null, never cancel at 0).

Add src/runs/token-budget.ts: pure tracker class - cumulative tokens per run, reserve logic (overRegularBudget vs overHardBudget), bad-attempt counter (reset on successful turn, increment on tool error), confident-completion flag.

Wire into the event bridge (src/runs/stream/): on turn_end, accumulate tokens from telemetry; on tool_result, update bad-attempts; emit 'budget.tokens' event per tool_use with {tool, delta}; when overRegularBudget and not confident-complete -> cancel with failure_reason 'token_budget'; when overHardBudget -> cancel unconditionally.
Expose the resolved budget on the run: fold maxTokens onto rendered_agent_json frontmatter at dispatch (same path as maxCostUsd override).

Tests: extend cost-cap.test.ts + add token-budget.test.ts (pure tracker); stream-bridge test asserting a run crossing the budget is cancelled with failure_reason token_budget, and a confident-completion turn inside the reserve finishes.
sections.acceptance: A run whose cumulative tokens cross 90% of maxTokens with no confident completion is cancelled (state cancelled, failure_reason token_budget). A run that signals confident completion inside the reserve finishes normally. maxBadAttempts terminates a run stuck in error loops. Malformed/absent maxTokens fails open (no cancellation). bun run check:all green. All acceptance scenarios still pass.
sections.behavior_invariant: A budget typo never cancels a run at zero tokens (fail open). Reserve never allows spending past the hard cap. Verification is additive - no new HTTP surface, no new dispatch primitive; enforcement lives in the existing stream bridge.

sections.context: Plan-run children are executed by one agent which then reaps itself succeeded - the implementer grades its own output. DeepMind x MIT: independent agents amplify errors 17.2x vs centralized 4.4x; self-grading is the centralized path. Files: src/plan-runs/coordinator.ts (child lifecycle), src/runs/reap/pipeline.ts (success path), src/registry/builtins/ (new verifier agent), src/registry/schema.ts if a verifier role key is needed.
sections.approach: Insert a verification stage between child-run success and plan-run advancement. After a child run reaches succeeded and its PR exists, dispatch a SECOND run with a dedicated verifier agent (different name, different model - e.g. deepseek-reasoner while the implementer is sapling - and instructions that forbid it from editing anything). The verifier receives the child's PR diff + the plan child's acceptance criteria; it returns a verdict (PASS/FAIL + findings) by writing a verdict to the plan-run child row via a small API extension (PATCH plan-run-child verdict) or by exiting with a convention. FAIL: mark the child failed, file a seed, do NOT advance the chain (planner may re-plan). PASS: advance as today. Self-grading blocked structurally: the verifier agent prompt explicitly forbids acting as the implementer, and the dispatch uses a different agent name than the child's implementer.
steps: Add builtin agent 'verifier' (src/registry/builtins/verifier.ts): runtime pi, model deepseek-reasoner (different from sapling implementer), system prompt = verify-only, no source edits, exit with verdict line.
Add a minimal API extension: PATCH /plan-runs/:id/children/:childId/verdict {verdict: pass|fail, findings} persisted on the child row (migration: plan_run_children.verdict, findings columns).

In the plan-run coordinator completion path (after child run succeeded + PR exists): dispatch the verifier run (agent=verifier, prompt includes the child PR url + acceptance criteria from the plan section), wait for verdict.
On FAIL: mark child failed with failure_reason 'verification_failed', file a seed (sd create, labels verification), leave the chain blocked; do NOT auto-advance.
On PASS: advance the chain as today. Log verification cost (runs.cost_usd on the verifier run) in the plan-run summary.
Tests: coordinator test asserting a FAIL verdict blocks advancement and files a seed; verifier agent smoke (acceptance scenario style). Gates: bun run check:all green.
sections.acceptance: Every plan-run child gets a verifier run after success and before advancement. FAIL verdict blocks the chain + files a verification seed. Self-grading is structurally impossible (different agent + prompt prohibition). Verifier never edits source (git diff empty on verifier runs). bun run check:all green.
sections.behavior_invariant: Verification is additive: no new dispatch primitive, reuse the run dispatch. A verifier failure must never silently pass. The verifier never writes code - only verdicts and findings.
